stories.title: Bond yields move relentlessly higher, as Wall Street wonders how much more tech stocks can take
stories.summary: Treasury yields have climbed steadily higher, and the pressure is starting to show in tech stocks. Investors are watching how much longer high-growth names can absorb rising yields before valuations crack.
stories.whyItMatters: Higher yields raise the discount rate on future earnings, the main risk to richly valued tech stocks in this market.
whatToWatch: Whether yields keep climbing or stabilize
How tech stocks trade if yields hit new highs
questions: What is driving the yield move — growth, inflation, or supply?
How much further can tech multiples compress before buyers step in?

stories.title: Stocks fall as higher oil prices and Treasury yields weigh
stories.summary: U.S. stocks declined as rising oil prices and climbing Treasury yields put pressure on the market. The combination of higher energy costs and higher borrowing costs has weighed on investor sentiment.
stories.whyItMatters: Rising oil and yields together squeeze both consumer spending power and corporate valuations, a double headwind for equities.
whatToWatch: Whether oil prices continue rising or ease back
Next moves in Treasury yields
questions: Is the oil price rise a supply story or a demand story?
How much of the yield rise is already priced into stocks?

stories.title: Nearly half the stocks in the S&P 500 are moving against the broader market
stories.summary: Close to half of the stocks in the S&P 500 are trading in the opposite direction of the index's overall move, according to CNBC. That points to a market where the headline number masks a split between winners and laggards underneath.
stories.whyItMatters: A market this divided suggests index-level gains or losses may not reflect what most individual stocks are actually doing, a warning sign for breadth-watchers.
whatToWatch: Whether market breadth improves or narrows further
Which sectors are driving the divergence
questions: Is this divergence concentrated in a few large-cap names or spread across sectors?
Does narrow breadth typically precede a broader pullback?

stories.title: MongoDB stock drops nearly 20% as CEO departs for Meta
stories.summary: Shares of MongoDB fell close to 20% after news that its CEO is leaving the company to join Meta. The abrupt leadership change has rattled investors in the database software company.
stories.whyItMatters: Losing a CEO unexpectedly raises questions about strategy continuity and can pressure a stock well beyond the initial selloff.
whatToWatch: Who MongoDB names as a successor
Whether the stock stabilizes or keeps sliding
questions: Why is the CEO leaving now, and what role will they take at Meta?
How does MongoDB's board plan to reassure investors?

stories.title: Nvidia announces historic $150 billion share buyback
stories.summary: Nvidia unveiled a $150 billion increase to its share buyback program, a move CNBC and MarketWatch both flagged as a major statement of confidence. The size of the buyback stands out even among mega-cap tech companies.
stories.whyItMatters: A buyback this large signals Nvidia's management sees the stock as undervalued and has substantial cash to return to shareholders, a bullish signal for the AI trade.
whatToWatch: Pace at which Nvidia executes the buyback
Market reaction in Nvidia shares in coming sessions
questions: How does this buyback compare with Nvidia's capital spending plans on AI infrastructure?
Will other AI-linked megacaps follow with similar announcements?

stories.title: Treasury yields rise as march to multiyear highs continues
stories.summary: Treasury yields rose again, extending a climb toward multiyear highs, according to CNBC. The steady upward move has become a persistent theme in fixed-income markets.
stories.whyItMatters: Rising Treasury yields raise borrowing costs across the economy and set the benchmark rate against which stocks and other assets are valued.
whatToWatch: Whether yields breach fresh multiyear highs
Any Fed commentary responding to the yield move
questions: What is driving the sustained rise — inflation expectations, growth, or issuance?
At what yield level would stocks face real valuation pressure?

stories.title: Judge rules feds can't withhold counterterrorism funds to force election changes
stories.summary: A judge ruled that the federal government cannot withhold counterterrorism funding from states as leverage to force changes to their election administration, per CNBC. The ruling addresses a dispute over conditions attached to federal funding.
stories.whyItMatters: The ruling limits how the federal government can use funding leverage over states, a precedent with implications beyond this specific dispute.
whatToWatch: Whether the ruling is appealed
How affected states respond to the decision
questions: Which states or funds were directly involved in this case?
What was the administration's stated rationale for the funding conditions?

stories.title: Sonos director Karen Boone sells $847,636 in company stock
stories.summary: Sonos director Karen Boone sold approximately $847,636 worth of company stock, according to a regulatory filing reported by Investing.com. The sale is disclosed as part of routine insider trading reporting.
stories.whyItMatters: Insider sales are watched by investors as a signal, though a single director sale of this size is not necessarily a sign of concern about the company's outlook.
whatToWatch: Whether other Sonos insiders report similar sales
Sonos stock reaction, if any, to the filing
questions: Was this sale part of a pre-arranged trading plan?
Does Boone retain a significant stake in Sonos after the sale?

stories.title: Oil prices pull back from highs on reports Saudi pipeline is ramping back up
stories.summary: Oil prices eased off their highs after reports that a Saudi pipeline is ramping back up, according to CNBC. The pullback suggests the earlier price gains were tied to supply concerns now easing.
stories.whyItMatters: Oil prices feed directly into inflation expectations and consumer costs, making supply-side swings like this one relevant to the broader rate outlook.
whatToWatch: Confirmation of the pipeline's full return to capacity
Whether oil prices continue easing or rebound
questions: What caused the pipeline disruption in the first place?
How much of the recent oil price rise was tied to this specific supply issue?

stories.title: OpenAI abandons plan to release upcoming model as safety concerns escalate
stories.summary: OpenAI has dropped plans to release an upcoming model after safety concerns escalated, according to CNBC. The company did not proceed with the release it had been preparing.
stories.whyItMatters: A major AI lab pulling back a planned release over safety concerns could shape the pace of competition and regulatory scrutiny across the AI sector.
whatToWatch: Whether OpenAI details the specific safety concerns
Any revised timeline or replacement plan for the model
questions: What specifically triggered the safety concerns?
Does this affect OpenAI's competitive position against rivals like Anthropic?

stories.title: Anthropic launches cheaper AI model, its second release since CEO's call for a slowdown
stories.summary: Anthropic released a lower-cost AI model, marking its second launch since its CEO called for a slowdown in AI development, according to CNBC. The release continues Anthropic's product cadence despite that earlier stance.
stories.whyItMatters: The launch highlights the tension between competitive pressure to keep shipping AI products and the industry's own stated safety concerns.
whatToWatch: Market and developer reaction to the new model's pricing
Whether Anthropic's CEO addresses the apparent tension publicly
questions: How does the new model's pricing compare with competitors like OpenAI?
What does 'slowdown' mean in practice if releases are continuing?

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit was more about domestic messaging than substance, CNBC newsletter says
stories.summary: CNBC's China Connection newsletter characterized the recent Trump-Xi summit as spectacle-heavy and oriented more toward domestic political messaging than substantive agreements. The framing suggests limited concrete outcomes from the meeting.
stories.whyItMatters: Markets watching U.S.-China relations for trade and tariff signals may need to temper expectations if the summit produced messaging rather than policy substance.

How markets react to the summit's actual substance versus its optics
questions: What, if anything, was concretely agreed at the summit?
